questions.prompt: Lines AB and CD intersect at E. Prove that ∠AEC ≅ ∠BED.
questions.prompt_markup: Lines AB and CD intersect at E. Prove that ∠AEC ≅ ∠BED.
questions.required_method: Use the two linear pairs that share ∠CEB, and the subtraction property of equality.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: (1) m∠AEC + m∠CEB = 180° (linear pair: A, E, B are collinear); (2) m∠CEB + m∠BED = 180° (linear pair: C, E, D are collinear); (3) so m∠AEC + m∠CEB = m∠CEB + m∠BED (substitution/transitive); (4) subtract m∠CEB. Alternative: the 180° rotation about E maps ray EA to ray EB and ray EC to ray ED. Invalid: "they look equal", measuring, or citing the theorem itself.
